title: Care for Those Who Cannot See It

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block in front of the blind, but fear your God. I am the LORD.'" - Lev 19:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at what makes these two acts possible: the deaf man cannot hear you curse him, and the blind man cannot see what you have placed in his path.

These are cruelties that cost nothing and carry no consequences. Nobody will ever know. The victim will not even understand what happened.

Which is exactly why God addresses them, and why the reason He gives is: but fear your God.

That phrase is the hinge. When no human accountability exists, only reverence for God restrains us. The person who behaves well solely because they might be caught will always mistreat those who cannot report them.

Test yourself here. How do you speak about people who will never hear it? The colleague discussed after they leave the room. The relative mocked in a family group chat. The customer service worker on the phone, treated as though they are not a person.

And what about stumbling blocks — the unhelpful advice, the withheld information, the small obstacle placed in someone's way because it serves you?

Character is what we are when the other person cannot see, cannot hear, and cannot respond. God can. And He is not indifferent.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you speak about people who will never hear it?
2. Have you ever made something harder for someone because you could?
3. What would change if you truly lived before God's watching eyes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see what others cannot. Guard my words about people who will never hear them, and keep me from making life harder for anyone who cannot answer back. Amen.
